Nicknamed "'''King Krut'''",{{cite news |url=https://mvc-sports.com/news/2021/3/6/arch-madness-game-7-loyola-65-indiana-state-49.aspx |title=Arch Madness Game 7: Loyola 65, Indiana State 49 |work=[[Missouri Valley Conference]] |date=March 6, 2021 |access-date=November 2, 2024 }} he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola Ramblers]]. Krutwig drew national attention after helping the [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|2017–18 Ramblers]] reach the [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament Final Four participants|Final Four]] of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]]. ==High school career== His older brother Conrad played collegiately at [[South Dakota Coyotes men's basketball|South Dakota]]. Cameron Krutwig attended [[Jacobs High School]] in [[Algonquin, Illinois]], where he was coached by Jimmy Roberts. As a junior, Krutwig averaged 17.7 points, 12.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.6 blocks, shooting 65 percent from the field. He led Jacobs to a Fox Valley Conference championship and its second Class 4A regional title in three seasons. In the state sectional semifinal loss to Rockford Auburn, Krutwig had 26 points and 14 rebounds. Krutwig was ranked Illinois's top center in his class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]]. He received more than 20 scholarship offers, and committed to [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola Chicago]] in August 2016.{{Cite news |last=Kantecki |first=Alex |date=August 3, 2016 |title=Boys basketball: Jacobs center Cameron Krutwig commits to Loyola |work=[[Northwest Herald]] |url=http://www.nwherald.com/2016/08/02/boys-basketball-jacobs-center-cameron-krutwig-commits-to-loyola/al1sacj |access-date=May 15, 2018 |archive-date=May 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516014823/http://www.nwherald.com/2016/08/02/boys-basketball-jacobs-center-cameron-krutwig-commits-to-loyola/al1sacj/ |url-status=dead }} As a senior, he led the team to a 30–2 record and a sectional championship. In the sectional final, he nearly posted a [[quadruple double]] with 20 points, 24 rebounds, 12 blocks and nine assists. ==College career== Krutwig became a starter three games into his freshman season and averaged 10.5 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |title=Loyola's Cameron Krutwig — an old-school, off-key singing 'goofball' — thriving in freshman season |work=March 27, 2018 |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-cameron-krutwig-20180327-story.html |access-date=May 15, 2018}} Coach [[Porter Moser]] praised him for his passing acumen and encouraged him to become more physical and score more when conference play began.{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |title=Loyola center Cameron Krutwig's 'old-school' ways translating to stellar freshman season |work=February 6, 2018 |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-cameron-krutwig-20180206-story.html |access-date=May 15, 2018}} Krutwig set season highs of 21 points and 13 rebounds in an 81–65 win over [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]] on January 13, 2018.{{Cite news |date=January 13, 2018 |title=Loyola-Chicago beats Bradley 81–65 on Krutwig's career game |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400989697 |access-date=May 15, 2018}} He was named to the Third Team All-Missouri Valley Conference and Freshman of the Year.{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |date=February 27, 2018 |title=Loyola's Clayton Custer named MVC player of the year |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-clayton-custer-20180227-story.html |access-date=March 2, 2018}} He received media attention for his [[Will Ferrell]] impressions and off-key Christmas caroling. In the NCAA Tournament, he contributed seven points and four assists against [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]] in a second-round victory. Krutwig helped Loyola to a rare Final Four appearance. Although the Ramblers lost to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] 69–57 in the Final Four, Krutwig led the team with 17 points.{{Cite news |last=Stevenson |first=Joe |date=March 31, 2018 |title=College basketball: Jacobs fans come out to support Krutwig, Ramblers |work=[[Northwest Herald]] |url=http://www.nwherald.com/2018/04/01/college-basketball-jacobs-fans-come-out-to-support-krutwig-ramblers/axybv4t |access-date=May 15, 2018 |archive-date=May 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516014756/http://www.nwherald.com/2018/04/01/college-basketball-jacobs-fans-come-out-to-support-krutwig-ramblers/axybv4t/ |url-status=dead }} Coming into his sophomore season, Krutwig was named to the Preseason Second Team All-MVC.{{Cite news |last=Hickey |first=Pat |date=October 18, 2018 |title=Evansville basketball teams picked to finish last in the Missouri Valley Conference |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/college/evansville/2018/10/18/missouri-valley-conference-basketball-voters-pick-ue-finish-last/1686522002/ |access-date=October 18, 2018}} He had a career-high 24 points in a 65–61 loss to [[Missouri State Bears men's basketball|Missouri State]] on February 17, 2019.{{Cite news |date=February 17, 2019 |title=Da Silva carries Missouri St. past Loyola of Chicago 65–61 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401089321 |access-date=November 7, 2019}} Krutwig averaged 14.8 points and 7.2 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |date=October 22, 2019 |title=Loyola isn't the favorite anymore. A look at college basketball in the city. |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-chicago-college-basketball-loyola-uic-depaul-northwestern-20191022-grw55sbunbgedjk5qfpqiyydlu-story.html |access-date=November 7, 2019}} He was named to the First Team All-MVC.{{Cite press release |title=Marques Townes headlines MVC specialty awards |date=March 5, 2019 |publisher=[[Missouri Valley Conference]] |url=http://mvc-sports.com/news/2019/3/4/arch-madness-marques-townes-headlines-mvc-specialty-honors.aspx |access-date=March 5, 2019}} On November 16, 2019, Krutwig matched his career-high of 24 points in an 85–68 win over [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]].{{Cite news |date=November 16, 2019 |title=Krutwig leads Loyola of Chicago over St. Joseph's 85–68 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170129 |access-date=December 22, 2019}} On December 18, Krutwig registered a [[triple-double]] of 22 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 78–70 win over [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]].{{Cite news |date=December 18, 2019 |title=Krutwig's triple-double leads Loyola-Chi. past Vandy |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-ncaa-lyc-van/krutwigs-triple-double-leads-loyola-chi-past-vandy-idUSMTZXEFCJQLJSRX |access-date=March 4, 2020}} At the conclusion of the 2019–20 regular season, Krutwig was named to the First Team All-MVC and received the second-most votes for player of the year behind [[A. J. Green (basketball)|A. J. Green]].{{Cite news |last=Hammond |first=Sean |date=March 3, 2020 |title=College basketball: Loyola's Krutwig earns First-Team All-MVC honors |work=[[Northwest Herald]] |url=https://www.nwherald.com/2020/03/03/college-basketball-loyolas-krutwig-earns-first-team-all-mvc-honors/a80asw/ |access-date=March 4, 2020 |archive-date=March 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304003549/http://www.nwherald.com/2020/03/03/college-basketball-loyolas-krutwig-earns-first-team-all-mvc-honors/a80asw/ |url-status=dead }} On January 11, 2021, in a game against [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]], Krutwig became just the fourth player in MVC history to amass 1,500 points, 800 rebounds and 300 assists. The other three players to have done so are [[College Basketball Hall of Fame]]rs [[Oscar Robertson]], [[Larry Bird]] and [[Hersey Hawkins]].{{Cite news |date=January 11, 2021 |title=Krutwig Helps Loyola Cut Down Indiana State, 58-48 |work=[[Loyola Ramblers]] |url=https://www.loyolaramblers.com/news/2021/1/11/mens-basketball-krutwig-helps-loyola-cut-down-indiana-state-58-48.aspx |access-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112041314/https://loyolaramblers.com/news/2021/1/11/mens-basketball-krutwig-helps-loyola-cut-down-indiana-state-58-48.aspx |url-status=dead }} At the close of the 2020–21 regular season, Krutwig was named the [[Missouri Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MVC Player of the Year]] and his third consecutive first-team All-MVC selection.{{cite press release|url=https://mvc-sports.com/news/2021/3/2/arch-madness-2021-mvc-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx|title=2021 MVC men's basketball al-conference team|publisher=[[Missouri Valley Conference]] |date=March 2, 2021 |access-date=March 2, 2021}} In the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Krutwig led the team with 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 5 assists in a second round upset victory over No. 1 seed [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{Cite news |date=March 21, 2021 |title=Cameron Krutwig, Loyola-Chicago stun top-seeded Illinois |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-ncaa-ill-lyc/cameron-krutwig-loyola-chicago-stun-top-seeded-illinois-idUSMTZXEH3LC168AH |access-date=April 25, 2021}} The Ramblers eventually fell to [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] in the Sweet Sixteen.{{Cite news |date=March 27, 2021 |title=Defensive-minded Oregon State knocks out Loyola Chicago in Sweet 16 |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-ncaa-lyc-ors/defensive-minded-oregon-state-knocks-out-loyola-chicago-in-sweet-16-idUSMTZXEH3RNCFV7T |access-date=April 25, 2021}} After the season, Krutwig announced he would not use his extra year of eligibility and instead declare for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{Cite news |last=Farris |first=Gene |date=April 22, 2021 |title=Loyola's Cameron Krutwig declares for NBA Draft |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2021/4/22/22397653/loyola-cameron-krutwig-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=April 25, 2021}} ==Professional career== On June 30, 2021, Krutwig signed his first professional contract with the [[Antwerp Giants|Telenet Giants Antwerp]] of the [[Pro Basketball League]].{{cite news |title=Former Loyola star Cameron Krutwig signs a pro contract with Antwerp in Belgium's EuroMillions League |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-cameron-krutwig-loyola-basketball-belgium-20210630-oyijay55z5fc3kzwvlfpsx7ahe-story.html |access-date=July 3, 2021 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=June 30, 2021}} On August 9, 2022, he signed with the [[Blackwater Bossing]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2022–23 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/blackwater-bossing-enlists-cameron-krutwig-as-import-a793-20220809|title=Blackwater taps Cameron Krutwig as import for Commissioner's Cup|website=Spin.ph|date=August 9, 2022|accessdate=August 10, 2022}} On November 29, Krutwig signed with [[Ibaraki Robots]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ibarakirobots.win/news/20221129_01_team/|title=#15 キャメロン・クラットウィグ選手 契約合意のご報告|publisher=Ibaraki Robots|language=Japanese|date=November 29, 2022|access-date=December 29, 2022}} In July 2023, Krutwig signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto]] of [[Spain]]'s [[LEB Oro]] basketball league, but was released after the team's ownership changed.{{cite news |last=Stevenson |first=Joe |url=https://www.shawlocal.com/northwest-herald/2024/06/26/basketball-jacobs-grad-cameron-krutwig-helps-spains-forca-lleida-earn-promotion-for-2025-season/ |title=Basketball: Jacobs grad Cameron Krutwig helps Spain’s Forca Lleida earn promotion for 2025 season |work=Northwest Herald |date=June 26, 2024 |access-date=November 2, 2024 }} He subsequently signed with [[Força Lleida CE]]. ==Personal life== Krutwig is a fan of the [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]].{{cite news |last=Mayer |first=Larry |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/loyola-basketball-star-krutwig-diehard-bears-fan-ncaa-tournament-sweet-16 |title=Loyola hoops star Krutwig a diehard Bears fan |work=[[Chicago Bears]] |date=March 24, 2021 |access-date=November 2, 2024 }} He is also a [[harmonica|harmonicist]], and cites the [[Bee Gees]], [[Hall & Oates]], [[Tears for Fears]], and [[Phil Collins]] among his favorite artists and influences.{{cite news |last=Norlander |first=Matt |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/court-report-cameron-krutwigs-harmonica-has-loyola-chicago-humming-along-as-it-tunes-up-for-run-at-big-dance/ |title=Court Report: Cameron Krutwig's harmonica has Loyola Chicago humming along as it tunes up for run at Big Dance |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 11, 2021 |access-date=November 2, 2024 }} Krutwig and his wife, Jess, were
